Hi Nina / Samir —

Quick answers + proposed patterns so the Mar 1 deep-dive can be tactical: 

SDK & auth -
- Python: full SDK (pip package) with native helpers for batching, streaming, and structured-output helpers.
- Go: lightweight official client (go modules) but if you prefer you can call the REST endpoints directly; the SDK adds client-side validation helpers.
- Auth: recommend short-lived JWTs issued by your IdP (OIDC) exchanged for Redwood access tokens, or API keys for initial POC. Private deployments support mTLS.

Reranker / cost pattern -
- Typical approach: retrieval (ANN) to get top N candidates from your vector DB -> single re-ranking step using a cross-encoder model call for final sorting. This is two steps but preserves quality.
- Option: for very latency-sensitive flows, use a lightweight rerank heuristic in the edge and only call cross-encoder for top K.

Structured output reliability
1) Schema-first decoding: include JSON Schema in the prompt and constrain generation using our constrained-decoding flag (token-level constraints + allowed keys).
2) Server-side validation: always run jsonschema validator on the model response. If invalid:
   - Retry pattern A (fast): retry with temperature=0 and deterministic decoding (same seed) up to 2x.
   - Retry pattern B (fallback): if still invalid, call the smaller deterministic model variant with stricter constraints.
   - Final fallback: return a structured error object with partial fields and an "error_code" so UI can gracefully degrade.
3) Idempotency & dedup: use request_id tokens so retries are safe. Store the last-valid KV cache entry for prefixes so repeated partial calls can reuse cached context.

Example (Python pseudo)
- auth header: headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {REDWOOD_TOKEN}", "X-Request-ID": req_id}
- constrained decode: client.generate(prompt, schema=example_schema, constraints=True, temperature=0.0)
- validate: try: jsonschema.validate(response, example_schema) except ValidationError: retry with temperature=0

Embeddings & reranker -
- Persist embeddings (128–1024 dims depending on model) into your existing vector DB (we have connectors for Faiss/Weaviate/Elastic).
- Re-ranker as a separate call: pass the top 50 retrieved candidates (ids + metadata) and use a cross-encoder to rescore. This avoids re-embedding at rerank time.
